claim: The actor hierarchy and its sizes: Actor 0x50 (ctor 0x60002C54), StageActor 0x284 (0x600002A0), CollisionActor 0x17B0, StateActor 0x17D4 (0x6000929C), MultiStateActor 0x17D8 (0x60009358), Enemy 0x189C (0x602A1A8C); CollisionActor and up carry a CollisionMgr at +0x288.

Actor::getProfileId 0x60002EEC is return this->profile->id: three instructions, ldr r0,[r0,#0xC] then ldr r0,[r0,#8]. The id lives in the Profile, so an actor built as profile 468 reports 468 regardless of what a mod calls it.

Actor::Actor 0x60002C54 takes its id from ActorMgr+0x6A38, its heap from sead::HeapMgr::getCurrentHeap, and its field_10 from ActorMgr+0x6A3C -- none from the spawn request. An unresolved parent id does not fail: the actor is built and flagged isDeleted (+0x13). field_2C is set to 0x30 (mov r0,#0x30 at 0x60002D28; str r2,[r4,#0x2c] at 0x60002D08).

ActorMgr::create 0x60008138 treats beforeCreate (vtable+0x10) as a three-way verdict: code = max(0, 3-verdict) is passed to afterCreate (vtable+0x18); code 3 goes to the live list, code 2 to the created-later path (Actor+0x12), anything else to the dead list with isDeleted set and a null return.

Allocation picks the heap by profile id: 443, 444, 855 and 856 are the players and get a heap named "PlayerHeap"; every other profile gets "ActorHeap" (0x600082CC). There is no flag for this -- a mod wanting the player heap must be one of those ids.

The actor id is generated before the build function runs: ActorMgr+0x6A38 = (ActorMgr+0x6A30) | (ActorMgr+0x6A28 << 22), so the high 10 bits and low 22 come from two separate counters. It is neither the spawn index nor the profile id.

StageActor::StageActor 0x600002A0 derives an actor collision half-extents from its Profile ActorInfo, not its model: field_204/208 = actorInfo->_18/_1A + 256.0, field_20C/210 = actorInfo->_1C/_1E + 80.0, field_1F4/1F8 = actorInfo->_10/_14 doubled. A replacement archive with a bigger model keeps the vanilla collision size unless ActorInfo changes.

StateMgr is four pointers (executer +0x0, nextState +0x4, currentMethodExecuter +0x8, lastState +0xC). ctor 0x60818168 ignores a first state whose id is -1 (that is NullState); execute 0x608181D4 runs at most one state transition per tick; changeState 0x60818224 ends the running state and builds the new executer immediately in the same call.

CollisionMgr::output is at CollisionMgr+0x8B0, so with the CollisionMgr at CollisionActor+0x288 it lands at actor+0xB38 -- exactly the byte the Goombrat ledge check 0x6033AA2C tests (raw encoding E5D40B38 = ldrb r0,[r4,#0xB38]) for FlagOnGround (1<<0).

claim: The slope height getter (0x6014C4A4) returns 0 unless FlagOnGround, then reads an edge index from CollisionMgr+0xA0C and returns the float at CollisionMgr+0xE18 + 56*index. The bound is 0..5 with a `cmp #5 / bxgt` returning 0, so a junk index yields no slope rather than an overread. The index arithmetic is rsb r0,r2,r2,lsl#3 then add r0,r1,r0,lsl#3, i.e. 56*index.

handleSpeed 0x60003624 turns slopes into sine-table lookups, never an atan2: the surface value it gets back is split into a table index, angleIndex = (surface >> 20) & 0xFF0, and a 24-bit fraction, (surface & 0xFFFFFF) / 2^24. The two are used to interpolate the sine table linearly at a 16-byte granularity, giving sin and cos of the slope angle.

handleSpeed rotates velocity rather than stepping position: dy = speed.y + speed.x*sin(angle), dx = speed.x*cos(angle). dx is halved when either slope-contact byte (+0x17A5 or +0x17A6) is set, then acceleration (+0x1788, +0x178C) and residual velocity (+0x1770) are added. So walking up a slope genuinely changes speed.y -- it is not a vertical snap.

CollisionMgr_init 0x6014B9E8 takes three nullable sensor templates and derives all four probes from them: blowSensor -> belowSensor (+0x958), aboveSensor -> aboveSensor (+0x94C), adjacentSensor -> both rightSensor (+0x934) and leftSensor (+0x940) with the left sensor c negated. A null template zeroes the sensor and sets its disable byte (+0x92C/+0x92B/+0x929/+0x92A respectively). Owner back-pointers are filled last: owner +0x894, position +0x89C, field_8A0/8A4/8A8, playerId +0x8AC.
evidence: decompile + paired str/strb offsets in the disassembly

claim: CollisionMgr_setSensor 0x6014BB58 writes slot id at +0x934+12*id, its disable byte at +0x929+id, a second flag at +0x925+id (always 1), and the manager markers +0x922/+0x923. The two byte arrays are only four apart, so ids above 3 would make them overlap; only slots 0-3 are addressed by this code, so the diagonal slots in the type layout are not reachable through setSensor.

handleSpeed applies friction after moving, not before: if CollisionActor+0x17AC is 1 the residual velocity at +0x1770 has +0x1774 subtracted from its magnitude and is clamped to zero rather than crossing it; if FlagOnGround is set the residual is cleared outright and +0x17AC reset. Applying velocity before decay is why an actor never stalls a frame early.

claim: HAZARD found and fixed in mods/slide_suit: wearingSuit() dereferences player+0x528, which is only valid on a player-sized allocation. sizeof(StageActor) is 0x284, so calling it on an arbitrary actor from the collider-overlap hook (which sees EVERY pair in the scene) reads past the end of the allocation. Fixed by having the onExecute hook record its BrosBase self in a 4-entry table and having the overlap hook only compare Actor* for pointer equality, never dereference. Verified in the emitted code: SlideSuit_doOverlap loads only [owner+0x40] and compares against the table.
evidence: reasoning about allocation size + objdump of the emitted doOverlap hook
